# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 17 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 17 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_017_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 9

**1** When she had finished all this she said to me, "Is there anything else you would like to see?" I was delighted at the prospect and said, "Lady, I would greatly like to see more." **2** She smiled and said, "Do you see the seven women surrounding the tower?" "Yes, I see them, my lady," I replied. "This tower," she said, "is being supported by these seven women. **3** The first, who grips the tower with her hands, is Faith. Through her God's chosen ones are saved. **4** The second, dressed in a long robe and exceedingly beautiful, is Continence. She is the daughter of Faith. Whoever follows her will be blessed in their life, for they abstain from all evil deeds, believing that if they refrain from all evil desire they will inherit eternal life." **5** "And who are the others, my lady?" "They are daughters of one another in succession: the first is Faith; the second, Continence; the third, Simplicity; the fourth, Knowledge; the fifth, Innocence; the sixth, Reverence; the seventh, Agape." **6** "And what part do they play in the life of the believers?" "Listen," she replied. "The one who follows these women and is able to hold fast to their works will dwell in the tower with the saints of God. **7** And why are they called daughters of one another? Because Continence is born of Faith; Simplicity of Continence; Innocence of Simplicity; Reverence of Innocence; Knowledge of Reverence; and Agape of Knowledge. Therefore their works are pure and holy and divine."

---

*LOGOS note: Agape preserved untranslated as a technical term — "love" in English lacks the theological weight of this Greek word in early Christian usage. The virtue genealogy is philosophically sophisticated: Agape as the final fruit of the whole moral sequence.*
